name: Comoros
tagline: An active volcano, and the fish that came back from the dead
summary: Karthala is one of the most active volcanoes in the world with a crater four kilometres across, the coelacanth was found alive off these islands after eighty million years, and Moroni's stone town is the least visited Swahili port on the coast.
when: May to October, the dry season. Cyclones are possible from December to March.

entries.caption: Karthala
entries.description: An active volcano with one of the largest craters on earth, walked up overnight.
entries.subject: the vast summit crater of Mount Karthala on Grande Comore

entries.caption: Three Islands and a Claim
entries.description: Grande Comore, Anjouan and Moheli, each volcanic, each different, and Mayotte disputed.
entries.subject: the volcanic coastline and black rock of Grande Comore

entries.caption: Livingstone's Fruit Bat
entries.description: A metre and a half across, found on Anjouan and Moheli and nowhere else.
entries.subject: a Livingstone's fruit bat hanging in forest canopy on Anjouan

entries.caption: Moheli Marine Park
entries.description: Turtles nesting in numbers, dugong, and humpbacks calving between July and October.
entries.subject: a green turtle coming ashore on a Moheli beach at night

entries.caption: The Volcanic Interior
entries.description: Karthala at 2,361 metres on Grande Comore, and Ntringui on Anjouan.
entries.subject: the forested volcanic interior of Anjouan

entries.caption: Anjouan's Cascades
entries.description: The Dziancoundre falls, and streams off the interior that run all year.
entries.subject: a waterfall falling through forest into a pool on Anjouan

entries.caption: No Rivers on Grande Comore
entries.description: The lava is too porous to hold a river — the water is in cisterns and Lake Sale.
entries.subject: the crater lake of Lac Sale beside the sea on Grande Comore

entries.caption: Black Sand and White
entries.description: Black volcanic sand on Grande Comore, and white on Moheli and Anjouan.
entries.subject: black volcanic sand and clear water on a Grande Comore beach

entries.caption: The Last Forest
entries.description: Karthala's forest, and Moheli's, hold the bats, the flying fox and the endemic birds.
entries.subject: cloud forest on the slopes of Mount Karthala

entries.caption: Climbing Karthala
entries.description: Overnight from Boboni, camping on the rim, and down the next day.
entries.subject: walkers camping on the crater rim of Karthala

entries.caption: Swahili, and Ylang-Ylang
entries.description: A Swahili island culture, and most of the world's ylang-ylang for perfume.
entries.subject: ylang-ylang flowers being picked on a Comorian plantation

entries.caption: The Grand Mariage
entries.description: The anda — a marriage that confers social rank, and can take a decade to afford.
entries.subject: a Grand Mariage procession with drummers and gold jewellery

entries.caption: Langouste and Pilao
entries.description: Lobster off the reef, pilao rice with cardamom, and vanilla and clove in everything.
entries.subject: grilled lobster with rice and coconut sauce

entries.caption: The Grand Mariage Season
entries.description: Weddings run through the dry season and take over whole villages for days.
entries.subject: a village square during a Grand Mariage celebration

entries.caption: Woodwork, Gold and Embroidery
entries.description: Carved doors, gold wedding jewellery, and the embroidered kofia cap.
entries.subject: an embroidered Comorian kofia cap and carved door detail

entries.caption: The Medina of Moroni
entries.description: A Swahili stone town with the Old Friday Mosque on the harbour since 1427.
entries.subject: the Old Friday Mosque on the harbour at Moroni

entries.caption: Nothing Listed, Much Standing
entries.description: No World Heritage sites, and Swahili stone towns on all three islands.
entries.subject: narrow stone alleys in the medina of Moroni

entries.caption: Moroni and Mutsamudu
entries.description: A volcanic harbour capital, and Anjouan's stone town under a citadel.
entries.subject: the stone town and citadel of Mutsamudu on Anjouan

entries.caption: Swahili Stone
entries.description: Coral-stone houses with carved doors, and the mosque architecture of the whole coast.
entries.subject: a carved wooden Swahili door in a coral-stone wall

entries.caption: The Harbour at Moroni
entries.description: Dhows unloading onto the rocks, and the mosque directly behind them.
entries.subject: dhows unloading at the rocky harbour below Moroni's mosque

entries.caption: Turtles and Shallow Reef
entries.description: Moheli's nesting beaches, and reef close enough in to snorkel from the sand.
entries.subject: children snorkelling over shallow reef off a Comorian beach

entries.caption: Volcano and Reef
entries.description: Karthala overnight, and diving the drop-offs on the same trip.
entries.subject: a diver over a coral drop-off in Comorian water

entries.caption: Small and Simple
entries.description: Guesthouses and a few beach hotels. Nothing at the top end anywhere.
entries.subject: a small beach guesthouse under palms on Moheli

entries.caption: Moheli's Community Park
entries.description: The marine park is run with the villages, and the turtle numbers have held because of it.
entries.subject: a community ranger recording turtle nests on Moheli

entries.caption: Volcano and Ocean
entries.description: Karthala's rim at first light, with the Indian Ocean on every side of it.
entries.subject: sunrise from the crater rim of Karthala over the ocean

entries.caption: The Coelacanth
entries.description: Caught off these islands in 1938, having been extinct for eighty million years.
entries.subject: a preserved coelacanth specimen in a Comorian museum case

entries.caption: Why Comoros
entries.description: An active volcano, a living fossil, and a Swahili stone town nobody visits.
entries.subject: a dhow off the volcanic coast of Grande Comore at sunset
